conventions.convention: The observed record retains the finite pattern label and its recorded coordinate projection. Empty coordinate tuples inhabit a one-point measurable space; a recorded zero placeholder does not assign a missing full-data value.

MCAR and MAR are almost-sure conditions relative to the specified full-data law and pattern projections. MAR requires a measurable observed-coordinate factor for every pattern; a family uses the same mechanism and factors across its laws. MNAR means MAR fails for at least one pattern.

The general observed-record reference uses patternwise pushforwards of an equivalent finite full-data reference. Missing-coordinate integral formulas require the separately stated product-reference hypotheses; empty blocks have unit mass.

Binary observed-law parameters are a=P(R=1) and b=P(R=1,Y=1), with 0≤b≤a≤1. Parameters are joint laws with these fixed observed masses, and MAR is assessed using each law's finite conditional response kernel.

Likelihood factorization assumes AC, a nonempty Cartesian parameter space Θ×Ψ, common MAR factors valid under every full-data law, and selected finite-valued density versions. Pointwise likelihood claims use these selected versions without asserting a common exceptional null set.

load_bearing.statement: The observed record is O=(R,W_obs(R)) in the disjoint union of the pattern-specific observed spaces; an empty coordinate tuple takes values in a one-point measurable space.

Relative to a specified full-data law, MCAR requires every pattern probability to be constant almost surely; MAR requires every pattern probability to be a measurable function of that pattern's observed projection almost surely; MNAR means MAR fails for at least one pattern.

Under AC, a full-data model dominated by a common sigma-finite positive measure and a supplied response probability kernel yields observed-pattern sublaws and full-data projected marginals dominated by the patternwise pushforwards of an equivalent finite reference. Selected pattern densities combine into an observed-record density; under the stated product-reference hypotheses, missing-coordinate integrals give density versions.

For 0≤b≤a≤1, the full-data means compatible with the binary observed law having response rate a and observed success mass b are exactly [b,b+1−a]. Without MAR the mean is unidentified when a<1 and identified as b when a=1. Under MAR it equals b/a for a>0 and remains unidentified for a=0.

Under AC, the response-model lemma's hypotheses, a nonempty Cartesian parameter space Θ×Ψ, and common MAR factors clipped to [0,1], the selected observed likelihood factors as ℓθ,ψ(r,x)=hψ,r(x)qθ,r(x). Positive response factors cancel from the stated likelihood ratios; profiling over the same Ψ multiplies qθ,r(x) by a θ-independent factor.

published_dependencies.used_for: Full-data coordinate spaces and observed-record measurable spaces.
Finite coordinate products and the empty-product convention.
Measurable full-data and response maps; the requirement that a real random variable be defined on the entire probability space.
Projected and observed-record pushforward laws.
Pointwise probability normalization and measurable response-kernel evaluations.
The supplied response mechanism as a conditional probability kernel, including null-state version freedom.
Parameter labels mapped to sampling laws, including joint laws as labels in the binary identification model.
Equality of binary observed-record laws across different full-data completions.
The full-data mean as a target function and the absence of a specified unconditional post-death score target.
Nonidentification from equal sampling laws with different means.
A fixed common sigma-finite full-data dominator.
AC-based selection of finite-valued nonnegative density versions and the limits of pointwise likelihood invariance.
The finite-measure exhaustion used to construct an equivalent finite reference.
Simultaneous selection of density representatives and the declared conditional-kernel existence assumptions.
Existence of patternwise marginal and observed-subprobability densities.
Finite-valued nonnegative representatives of the positive-measure density classes.
Measurable missing-coordinate integrals and their density identities under the explicit product-reference hypotheses.
Extending pushforward integration identities from indicators and simple functions to nonnegative measurable functions.
Passing simple approximations through the integrals in MAR factorization.
Simple-function integration against a density; the consuming proof explicitly extends this to nonnegative functions by monotone convergence.
The taxonomy definition's remark about obtaining a response mechanism from a joint law under AC.
The same remark's construction of a conditional kernel on the full-data value space.
